claims.claim: The skill may be used only after explicit user approval to inspect, debug, or interact with a page open in Chrome.
The documented command surface covers target listing, screenshots, accessibility snapshots, page inspection, navigation, input, and daemon shutdown.
The skill forbids automatic Lightpanda fallback and requires explicit approval before connecting to another browser or retrying there.
On non-Windows systems, the CLI applies a private process mask and creates its runtime directory with owner-only permissions.
The CLI's Lightpanda error response states that fallback did not run automatically and prints manual steps beginning with asking the user.
Unsupported Lightpanda methods route to the fallback-required message and return a failing process status instead of retrying elsewhere.
Opening a new tab reports that the tab needs Chrome's Allow debugging approval on first access.
